RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the December 23, 2004/Pausa 2, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal;
Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Mines; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs; Personnel,
Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Science and
Technology; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Small Scale Industries; Space; Statistics and
Programme Implementation)
Total number of questions — 20
Constitution of Asian Economic
Community
*321. DR. AKHILESH DAS : Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have initiated
steps towards constitution of an Asian
Economic Community on the lines of
European Union (EU);
(b) if so, the precise constitution and
modus operandi of the contemplated
Economic Community and India's role
therein; and
(c) the progress made in this regard, so
far?
Funds for poverty eradication
*322. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether inadequate funds are
blocking developmental goals to reduce
poverty to half by the year 2015;
(b) whether the funds released by
Government are not reaching to the poor;
and
(c) if so, the action proposed to step up
efforts to remove economic hurdles, to
build up proper administration for
fulfilment of millenium goals to eradicate
poverty?
Security deposit in rural areas under
NOIDA Telephone Exchange
†*323. SHRI VEER SINGH: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that for
registration of telephone, a security amount
of Rs. 3000/- is being charged, instead of
Rs. 500/-, from the consumers of rural
categories coming under NOIDA
Telephone General Manager;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) if not, the details of the matter?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

97
Extradition treaty with Portugal
*324. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) Government efforts to tie a formal
extradition treaty with Portugal; and
(b) what efforts have been taken by
Government to ensure that more Indian
criminals in other countries like UAE,
Bangkok etc. are also handed over?
Jobs to unemployed youths
*325. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of educated unemployed
persons in the country, State-wise;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
are forming a scheme for providing jobs to
unemployed educated youths in the
country; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Single window facility for
NRIs
*326. DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS
INDIAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have planned
a comprehensive single window facility for
Non-Resident Indians and also special
courts and a 23 point programme that will
address pressing issues concerning the
NRIs;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) to what extent these proposals have
been finalized and announced; and
(d) to what extent Government have
been able to help the NRIs in a more
systematic manner?
Child labour in cotton seed
farms
*327. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether thousands of children are
working under hazardous conditions in the
cotton seed farms for various MNCs in
Andhra Pradesh;
(b) whether a number of children have
died or became seriously ill due to exposure
to pesticides;
(c) whether Government have issued
any instructions to these companies for
restricting them from hiring child
labourers; and
(d) the action taken by Government
against the cotton seed companies
employing child labourers?
Linking India, Myanmar and
Thailand by road
†*328. SHRIMATI SAVITA
SHARDA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
consideration of Government to link India,
Myanmar and Thailand by road routes;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when a final decision in this
regard would be taken?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

98
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Criteria for giving reservation to SC/
STs, and OBCs
*329. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the system adopted while giving
reservation to SC/STs and OBCs in Civil
Services and competitive examinations
held by UPSC, SSC, etc.;
(b) whether it is a fact that while
allocation is made to SC/STs and OBCs,
even meritorious reserved category
candidates are also included in it; and
(c) whether Government would change
this system of allocation for the benefit of
the SC/STs and the OBCs?
Upgradation of certain ESI hospitals in
Karnataka
*330. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of LABOUR
AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Karnataka Government
have sought upgradation of Belgaum,
Chitradurga, Davangere, Haveri and Hubli
ESI hospitals in Karnataka;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal; and
(c) the present status of the above
proposal?
Condition of Devidhar Telephone
Centre
†*331. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the condition of Devidhar
Telephone Centre under Roh ru
Telephone Exchange in Shimla District
is very bad;
(b) whether the present range of BSNL
tower is limited to main Bazar Rohru only;
(c) if so, whether Government propose
to set up one additional BSNL tower
between Sima and Badiyara so that more
people would be benefited; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
New coal deposits
†*332. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER 
   SINGH MAJITHA:
  SHRI RAVI SHANKAR 
  PRASAD:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that new coal
deposits have of late been explored in the
country by the Geological Survey of India;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
details of the States having the deposits
alongwith the quantity thereof; and
(c) the details of the schemes
Government have worked out for mining
the said deposits?
CBI raids
*333. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of PERSONNEL, PUBLIC
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the CBI conducted nation-
wide raids on corrupt Government officials
and a large number of  businessmen in
September, 2004;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the names of Government officials
raided by the CBI;

99
(d) the details of seizures made from
these Government officials; and
(e) the departmental action so far taken
against these officials?
Regional Passport Office
at  Aizawl
*334. SHRI LALHMING LIANA: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
contemplating opening of a Regional
Passport Office at Aizawl;
(b) if so, the action taken thereon; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
India-ASEAN Summit
*335. SHRI AJAY SINGH
CHAUTALA:
SHRI DARA SINGH:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Prime Minister
attended the Third India-ASEAN Summit
held at Vientiane in Laos on November,
29-30, 2004;
(b) if so, the details of discussions and
the outcome thereof, indicating names of
other countries which participated at the
Summit;
(c) whether Indian Prime Minister also
held bilateral meetings with his counterpart
of China, Japan, etc. on the sidelines of
Summit;
(d) if so, with what results; and
(e) whether India's proposal of a road
and rail link between India and South-East
Asia articulated at the above mentioned
Summit?
Functioning of High Commissions of
India and Pakistan
*336. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that both India
and Pakistan have taken a decision to
restore their High Commission staff at New
Delhi and Islamabad to the original status;
(b) if so, the reasons for pendency of
thousands of applications for VISA in our
High Commission at Islamabad; and
(c) if not, the reasons and the
obstructions in the way of normalising the
functioning of the High Commissions in
both countries?
Corruption free Governance
*337. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have any short
term or long term plan that are both
pragmatic and actionable to usher the
country into an era of corruption free
governance;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Disputes referred by Uttaranchal
Government regarding allotment of
employees
*338. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
PRIME MINISTER  be pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Uttaranchal has referred certain disputed
issues to the Central Government for
decision with regard to matter of  allotment
of employees after the formation of the
State; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

100
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 17th December, 2004 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 26, 1926 (Saka)
(b) if so, the details of such referred
cases alongwith the steps taken by the
Central Government in this regard?
Bypasses on National Highways in
Kerala
*339. SHRI ABDUL WAHAB
PEEVEE: Will the Minister of  SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any request has been
received from the Government of Kerala
for early construction of bypasses on
National Highways in Kerala;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the status report of work started in
each case; and
(d) by when the entire construction
work is likely to be completed?
Indian fishermen in
Pakistani jails
*340. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
Government have not honoured its
promise of rescuing 406 Indian
fishermen from Pakistani jails;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Pakistani
Marine Guards have seized 10 more boats
and 60 fishermen from Gujarat;
(c) whether some of the fishermen are
languishing in Pakistani jails for over three
years; and
(d) if so, the steps Government
propose to take to rescue those Indian
fishermen?

RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the December 23, 2004/Pausa 2, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal
and Mines; Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs;
Labour and Employment; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Science and
Technology; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Small Scale Industries; Space; Statistics and
Programme Implementation)
Total number of questions — 155
Promotion of coir industry
2210. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the steps Government have taken to
promote coir industry through Coir Board
in non-traditional zone;
(b) the steps taken to maximize husk
collection in non-traditional zone; and
(c) whether Government propose to
merge Coconut Development Board and
Coir Board to maximize husk collection in
general and non-traditional zone in
particular?
Margin Money Scheme
2211. SHRI SUDARSHAN
AKARAPU: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Khadi and Village
Industries Commission (KVIC) had
launched Margin Money Scheme for
setting up agro based and rural industries;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of agro and rural
industries assisted under the scheme during
the last three years, State-wise; and
(d) the total amount sanctioned and
spent under the scheme?
REGP in Tamil Nadu
2212. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have set up
any agro-rural industries in Tamil Nadu
under Rural Employment Generation
Programme during the last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the fund allocation;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps taken by Government
to further promote these sectors in
Tamil Nadu?

487
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Cottage industries in Bihar
†2213. SHRIMATI  KUM KUM RAI :
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the cottage industries in the areas belonging
to SCs/STs/most backward classes have to
face host of problems in the State of Bihar;
(b) if so, the steps taken or proposed to
be taken in near future for the promotion
of cottage industries;
(c) the number of small scale industries
in Bihar at present, area-wise;
(d) whether Government have taken any
initiative to boost up the setting up of small
industrial units in the backward and tribal
areas of Bihar; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Industries set up under NPRI
2214. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the number of rural industrial
clusters set up in the States of Bihar,
Jharkhand, Orissa and Rajasthan under the
National Programme on Rural
Industrialisation (NPRI);
(b) the financial assistance provided to
these States under the said scheme and the
outcome thereof; and
(c) the institutional arrangement made
to implement NPRI in these States?
Funds for Khadi and Village Industries
2215. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the amount of funds earmarked for
research and development for promoting
Khadi and Village Industries (KVI) during
the last three years and the outcome thereof,
State-wise;
(b) whether Government intend to
enhance allocation meant for R&D for
KVI; and
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise?
Development of coir industries
2216. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coir Board
has asked for Centre's help for development
of this sector on the lines of Bamboo
industry;
(b) whether it is also a fact that this
industry has immense potential in the
international market; and
(c) if so, the details of the action plan
of Government to develop this industry to
generate additional employment and
improve the economy of this sector?
Selection criteria of BARC Training
School, Mumbai
2217. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA:
SHRI NAND KISHORE
YADAV:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Engineering Graduates and
Science Post-graduates have been
interviewed this year for selection to
training of OCES and DGFS at BARC
Training School, Mumbai, for appointment
of Scientific Officer 'C';

488
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, whether merit performance in
written test and GATE score has been
ignored for selected persons;
(c) if so, whether there is resentment
amongst meritorious candidates against
this selection criteria and have demanded
removal of favouritism through written test
by UPSC instead of interview by BARC;
and
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Fast Breeders Reactors
2218. DR. K. KASTURIRANGAN :
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have any plans
for establishing fast breeder reactors for
nuclear power generation in addition to the
presently operating pressurized heavy
water reactors;
(b) if so, the details of their number,
the power capacity and the schedules for
implementation;
(c) whether Government have plans for
upscaling the present design of 500 MW
power capacity of the fast breeder reactors;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Power generation from atomic power
2219. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) the States in which sites for power
generation from Atomic Energy have been
identified during the years 2001-04;
(b) whether any site has been identified
in the State of Madhya Pradesh also, if so,
the details thereof; and
(c) if any site has been identified in
Madhya Pradesh, the funds provided to the
State for power generation from atomic
energy since the year 2002?
New Atomic Power Plants
2220. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in the wake
of success of peace process initiated for
cordial relations with neighbouring
countries, the chances of use of atomic
energy for peaceful purposes have
brightened;
(b) if so, the quantity of atomic energy
likely to be made available for use in
medical purposes and production of power;
and
(c) the details of new atomic power
plant likely to be established in the near
future, if any?
Completion of Kaiga Atomic Power
Project
2221. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether technical snags are delaying
the completion of Kaiga Atomic Power
Project in Karnataka;
(b) the extent of overall cumulative
physical progress on Kaiga Project
achieved by the end of 2003; and
(c) the target dates for the plant to go
critical?
Efficiency of Atomic Power Plants
†2222. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a very small

489
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
part of total power generation of the
country is being produced from atomic
energy;
(b) if so, the main reasons therefor and
the status of India as compared to other
countries in power generation from atomic
energy;
(c) whether efficiency of atomic power
plants in the country is low; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken by Government to increase
atomic power generation in the country?
Royalty on coal
2223. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) whether coal royalty was not revised
on the due date in the year 2003, if so, the
reasons for the same;
(b) the amount of royalty that the States
lost from that year onwards, State-wise and
year-wise; and
(c) whether Government are
considering to compensate the States for
the losses sustained on that account?
Diesel consumed in Northern
Coalfields Limited
2224. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity and cost of diesel
consumed monthly for running the heavy
machines in Northern Coalfields Ltd.
(NCL) Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh during
the last three years;
(b) whether Government are aware that
diesel worth lakhs of rupees is being
pilfered every month;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government propose to
conduct an enquiry in this regard;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Road map for coal sector
2225. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
constituted an Expert Committee to carry
out a comprehensive review and draw up a
road map for the coal sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the composition and terms of
reference of the Committee; and
(d) by when the Committee is likely to
submit its report?
Irregularities in the sale of coal
†2226. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to conduct C.B.I.
investigation in the matter related to
irregularities found in the sale of coal;
(b) if so, the comprehensive details of
irregularities committed in the sale of coal;
and
(c) the officials responsible for the said
irregularities?

490
Coal linkage in Jharkhand
†2227. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering any proposal to grant 'coal
linkage' to the industries going to be set up
in Jharkhand;
(b) whether any talks have been held
with the Industry Minister of Jharkhand;
and
(c) if so, the policy of Government in
this regard?
Taking over of Coal Mines in
Jharkhand by private companies
†2228. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to hand over some Coal Mines to the
private companies;
(b) if so, the number of such mines in
Jharkhand;
(c) the names of such private
companies; and
(d) the present status thereof?
Deeming mines for captive use
2229. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of
MINES be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of mines ore-wise
held on lease to industries for captive use,
for value addition without deeming the
mines as captive and to others; and
(b) considering that there is a need for
value addition within the country, whether
Government would consider amending the
laws to give priority to industries deeming
mines for captive use?
Deposits of lower grade coal
2230. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the disparity between the
higher and lower grades of coal has
increased disproportionately over the last
three decades and more; and
(b) if so, whether there is any proposal
for applying correctives to ensure that
States having deposits of lower grade coal
are not discriminated against?
Import of coal
2231. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coal Industry
has become an ailing industry and as such
coal is being required to be imported from
other countries;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether any steps are being
considered to improve the functioning of
the industry; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Selling of coal by private parties
2232. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to allow
private parties to sell coal in retail; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and by when
it is likely to be finalized and implemented?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

491
Postal service in every Panchayat
†2233. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
for providing postal service in every
Panchayat of country under which branch
post-office, sub post-office or post-office
would be set up;
(b) if so, by when it would be done,
and if not, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the numbers of such Gram
Panchayats at present, specially in
Himachal Pradesh, which still do not have
postal service facilities and by when these
facilities would be provided in these
Panchayats?
Modernisation of communication
facilities in Maharashtra
2234. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
expand capacity of the existing telephone
exchanges by providing modern
communication facility in Maharashtra
during the year 2003-04;
(b) if so, the details thereof,
district-wise; and
(c) the funds provided by Government
for the said period?
Defacing of Indian websites by
Pakistan
2235. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that hacking or
defacing of the Indian websites by Pakistan
is on the rise;
(b) if so, the details of websites hacked
by Pakistan during the last three years,
year-wise; and
(c) the action Government have
contemplated in this regard?
Failure of Speed Post Service
2236. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for the failure of the
Speed Post Service in attracting adequate
posts to obtain a good market share;
(b) whether it is a fact that the Speed
Post Service did not earn a reputation for
speed or reliability;
(c) whether any study has been done to
obtain the causes of failure of the Speed
Post Service in the country;
(d) what steps are proposed to ensure
that the Speed Post Service becomes more
efficient and reliable; and
(e) the details of measures proposed to
improve the Speed Post Service?
E-Governance
2237. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have initiated a pilot scheme for the spread
of e-Governance in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any scheme related to
 e-governance has been launched/due to be
launched in Tamil Nadu; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

492
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Dwindling telephone market share of
MTNL and BSNL
2238. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether on account of strident
promotion by private players of their
services and products, the telephone market
share of MTNL and BSNL is dwindling
continuously;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether private players offer a
number of added features at competitive
rates in both fixed, wireless and mobile
phones, which Government sector is unable
to offer;
(d) if so, what measures are
contemplated to win back the customers;
(e) whether MTNL, Delhi Telephone
Directory has not been published for the
last many years; and
(f) if so, by when it is likely to be
issued?
Sale of BSNL recharge coupon in
Karnataka
2239. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
